s.t:
You will co-lead as LANT's focal point in CI construction polices/processes reviews to determine changes and additions necessary to meet current requirements.
You will provide technical reach back support for FEAD/ROICCs for such construction-related matters.
You will streamline, develop, and keep current standardized position descriptions at various GS grade levels for entry, advanced, and senior CM and ET positions.
You will research and coordinate opportunities for centralized-training events including on-site facilitators/instructors and/or creation of online construction-related training courses to enhance workforce knowledge and technical skills.
Your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-12 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Understanding of engineering/architectural concepts and practices; 2) Administering contracts, responding to correspondence, preparing government reports, conducting meetings, and monitoring quality and safety; 3) Understanding of various construction contract types (e.g., design-bid-build, design-build, MACC, ID/IQ, JOC); 4) Understanding of computer applications, including word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, and scheduling software (such as Primavera); 5) Communicating effectively, both orally and in writing, with a wide range of individuals, from junior staff to senior leaders; 6) Developing creative and technically sound solutions to complex and unusual problems where standard processes may not apply; 7) Managing multiple priorities and ensuring that project deadlines and budgets are met.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Anthropic's Global Workplace & Real Estate team is delivering a rapidly expanding global portfolio — including full-building offices at the scale of ~450,000 SF that combine commercial kitchens, executive briefing centers and event space, high-end amenities, and the elevated power, cooling, and security infrastructure our work requires.

We're hiring a Real Estate Construction Manager to lead the technical delivery of these projects from pre-construction through closeout and to serve as our primary technical counterpart to general contractors, design teams, and specialty vendors.
This is a hands-on construction leadership role, not a design role. You will own how our projects get built: delivery method and contracting strategy, GC selection and oversight, MEP and specialty-systems coordination, cost and schedule control, and commissioning.

Executing the design direction is set by the Global Head of Real Estate & Workplace and our architects. You will also lead and develop a team of project managers delivering across the global portfolio. This role reports to the Global Head of Real Estate & Workplace.

Pre-construction & technical delivery
Lead pre-construction on complex buildouts: constructibility and design/drawing reviews, MEP and structural coordination, estimating support, value engineering, and development of the GMP or bid package.
Recommend and own the delivery method and contracting strategy for each project (e.g., GMP, lump sum, CM-at-risk, design-assist), matching the approach to scope, schedule, and risk.
Read and interpret architectural, structural, and MEP drawings and specifications; surface gaps, conflicts, and risk before they reach the field.
Coordinate technically demanding scopes — commercial kitchens (Type I hoods, make-up air, grease and UL300 fire-suppression systems, utility upsizing), high-performance AV and acoustics for executive and event spaces, server/IDF rooms with redundant power and supplemental cooling, elevated power density, and integrated physical security.
Manage permitting and inspections with authorities having jurisdiction across multiple markets and labor environments.
Construction execution, quality & closeout
Oversee construction from mobilization through closeout across multiple concurrent projects, holding general contractors accountable to schedule, budget, safety, and quality.
Run the technical processes that keep a job on track: RFIs, submittals and shop drawings, ASIs, and BIM/clash coordination across trades; lead owner-architect-contractor and trade-coordination meetings.
Conduct site visits to monitor progress, safety, and quality control; enforce inspection protocols and punch-list management.
Drive commissioning and closeout — systems commissioning (including kitchen exhaust/MUA balancing, BMS, and life-safety), TCO/CO, as-builts, O&M manuals, warranties, attic stock, and owner training.
Ensure compliance with local building codes, ADA requirements, and Anthropic's sustainability goals.
General contractor, vendor & contract management
Serve as the primary point of contact for general contractors, subcontractors, and external project managers, holding them to clear communication and accountability.
Lead GC selection end to end: pre-qualification/RFQ, RFP/ITB, bid leveling and scope normalization, scope-gap detection, and award — and structure the contract (GMP fee, general conditions/requirements, allowances, contingencies, qualifications, and exclusions).
Negotiate and administer contracts with contractors, vendors, and consultants; manage GC performance throughout construction, including schedule adherence, change-order management, safety compliance, and closeout.
Determine which trades and specialty vendors to carry under the GC vs. hold owner-direct, and manage critical long-lead vendors (kitchen equipment, AV, architectural millwork, switchgear/generator).
Develop and maintain landlord and property-management relationships to facilitate approvals and ongoing operations.
Cost & commercial controls
Build and own detailed budgets by trade/CSI division — separating hard costs, soft costs, FF&E, technology, allowances, and escalation — and manage design, construction, and GC contingencies deliberately.
Review and approve budgets, change orders, and invoices, including schedule-of-values setup, pay-application review (e.g., AIA G702/G703), retainage, and lien waivers, providing professional pushback to protect Anthropic's interests.
Govern the change-order process (PCO to CO, markups, substantiation) and distinguish legitimate changes from scope gaps the contractor should have carried.
Lead value engineering that protects scope and design intent; maintain cost forecasting and reporting throughout each project.
Team leadership

TECHNICAL PROFICIENCY: Technically proficient with various software programs such as construction management software and Microsoft suite of products (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.) Use project and contract management systems in the daily operation of the business.

You will serve as a GENERAL ENGINEER - Senior Construction Manager and be responsible to serve as a Construction/Design Project Manager within a multi-disciplinary architectural and engineering team on design-build projects. Being a Coast Guard civilian makes you a valuable member of the Coast Guard team.

Typical work assignments include: Lead, manage, and direct complex engineering and architectural projects by adapting standard precedents, modifying established practices, and developing innovative solutions to resolve highly diverse and technical engineering challenges.

Direct and execute all assigned projects as a technical authority, independently providing expert recommendations and policy guidance to ensure final submissions are viable, technically accurate, and accepted with minimal revision.

Direct the interpretation of broad, non-specific technical and regulatory policies by applying seasoned judgment to deviate from traditional practices, resolve unprecedented challenges, and establish new engineering methodologies.

Command and execute the resolution of complex, unprecedented engineering challenges by interpreting broad regulatory policies, departing from traditional practices, and establishing new technical standards.

Avert and resolve critical, highly unusual engineering problems and policy gaps by pioneering innovative technical approaches and initiating proactive administrative and socioeconomic actions to prevent project delays and cost escalations.
Basic Requirements: This position has a positive Education Requirement in addition to at least one year of Specialized Experience or substitution of education for experience or combination (if applicable) in order to be found minimally qualified. Transcripts must be submitted with your application package.

You MUST meet the following requirements: Degree: Engineering.

To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.

OR Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering.

The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1, or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.

Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.

For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions.

Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.

Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A.

The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.

Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

(The above examples of related curricula are not all-inclusive.) To qualify at the GS-13 grade level, your resume must demonstrate at least one (1) full year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-12 grade level in the federal sector.

Specialized experience is experience that has equipped you with the ability, skill, and knowledge to successfully perform the duties of this position and is typically in or related to this line of work. Examples of specialized experience include performing the following types of tasks on a regular basis.

Knowledge of specialty areas in civil engineering and construction management sufficient to apply new developments and theories to critical and novel problems.

Architectural/ engineering contracting methods, precedents, and standards Knowledge of design, construction, and cost estimating techniques to enable determination of technical feasibility and estimated costs for shore and in-water materials, and services.

NOTE: All experience statements (i.e., duties, specialized experience, or related applicable assessment) copied from this announcement and pasted into your resume will not be considered as a demonstration of your qualifications for this position. NOTE: Education cannot be substituted for experience at this grade level.

National Service Experience (i.e., volunteer experience): Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Job Description
Olsson has an exciting opportunity to work directly with one of the world's largest technology companies. As a Construction Project Manager, you will lead the construction closeout process for complex data center projects, ensuring all documentation, redlines, as-builts, and turnover deliverables are completed accurately, on time, and to the highest quality standards.
In this role, you will oversee closeout activities from field verification through final turnover, managing redline processes, conducting as-built audits, performing QA/QC reviews of project deliverables, and coordinating with contractors, trade partners, and project stakeholders. You will be responsible for driving accountability, identifying and resolving issues that could impact project schedules, and ensuring all closeout requirements are met.
The ideal candidate possesses a strong understanding of mechanical and electrical systems, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment while managing multiple priorities. Success in this role requires strong communication skills, technical problem-solving abilities, and a proven track record of delivering complex projects with a high degree of quality and accuracy.

Having ownership in the work you do.
Using your talents to positively affect communities.

Lead and manage construction closeout activities for large-scale data center projects.
Oversee and coordinate the collection, review, and approval of redlines, as-builts, O&M manuals, warranties, and other closeout documentation.
Perform field verification audits to validate as-built conditions and ensure documentation accuracy.
Conduct QA/QC reviews of project deliverables to verify completeness, consistency, and compliance with project requirements.
Hold contractors, trade partners, and stakeholders accountable for meeting closeout milestones and documentation requirements.
Monitor closeout schedules, identify risks, and proactively drive corrective actions to maintain project timelines.
Utilize knowledge of mechanical and electrical systems to review technical deliverables and resolve discrepancies.
Communicate project status, risks, and action items to internal and external stakeholders.
Continuously improve closeout processes and documentation standards to support efficient project turnover.

Job Description Are you an experienced construction project leader with the commercial acumen to deliver complex infrastructure projects while managing the expectations of lenders, investors and key stakeholders?
We are looking for an experienced Senior Construction Project Manager to fulfil the Client / Employer’s Representative role across Elgin’s utility-scale solar PV, BESS and co-located PV/BESS projects.

The role is focused on leading multidisciplinary project teams within a single Elgin delivery framework, ensuring that finance, legal, engineering, procurement, construction, operations, route-to-market and external adviser inputs are coordinated into one clear project position from late stage development / FID through construction, commissioning, commercial operations and handover to Asset Management.

Particular emphasis will be placed on lender, investor, SPV governance and internal delivery interfaces.
This role requires significant project and contract management experience, including direct involvement in project finance processes, lender due diligence, conditions precedent, drawdown evidence, lender reporting, waivers / consents and coordination with lender technical advisers.

The successful candidate will need specific experience with FIDIC based Construction Contracts, strong commercial judgement, disciplined contract administration capability and the ability to translate project delivery status into clear funding, governance and decision-making outputs.
To be successful in the role, you will have experience representing a client, employer, sponsor or SPV in the delivery of complex infrastructure or renewable energy projects. You will be commercially astute, highly organised, confident leading multidisciplinary project teams through a common governance and delivery framework, and capable of engaging credibly with lenders, investors, advisers, contractors, shareholder forums and senior internal stakeholders.

Fulfil the Client / Employer’s Representative role for allocated projects, ensuring Elgin’s SPV, governance, commercial and contractual obligations are actively managed from FID through COD and handover.
Lead project and contract management on project-financed assets, coordinating lender processes including conditions precedent, drawdown evidence, lender technical adviser queries, lender reporting, waivers / consents and funding milestone submissions.
Administer and manage high-value EPC, ICP and related project contracts, including notices, variations, claims, payment applications, completion milestones, liquidated damages, defects and close-out obligations.
Maintain disciplined project controls across programme, budget, cash flow, risk, actions, decisions and change, ensuring transparent reporting to senior management, SPV governance bodies, lenders and investors.
Act as the primary project coordination point between Elgin’s internal project team, finance, legal, procurement, engineering, construction, operations, route-to-market and external advisers, ensuring that all workstreams operate from one integrated delivery plan, one risk position and one set of decision requirements.
Lead and manage multidisciplinary internal project teams within Elgin’s agreed delivery framework by setting priorities, clarifying accountabilities, managing dependencies, aligning workstreams to project milestones and escalating decisions in a timely and structured manner.
Manage the relationship and reporting cadence with project finance lenders, equity investors, shareholder representatives, lender technical advisers and other key finance-facing stakeholders, including preparing and presenting clear, decision-ready updates for shareholder forums and related governance meetings.
Oversee contractor, owner’s engineer and technical adviser interfaces to ensure delivery evidence, technical outputs and contractual positions support Elgin’s funding, governance and employer obligations.
Proactively identify commercial, contractual, programme and financing risks, develop mitigation plans and ensure issues are escalated with clear options, recommendations and decision requirements.
Support tendering, contract negotiation and commercial strategy by ensuring delivery arrangements are bankable, financeable, contractually robust and aligned with lender / investor expectations.

s.h: Your profile What you will need
s.t:
Degree in project management, construction management, engineering, or similar.
Extensive experience in infrastructure, renewables, power, energy storage or comparable capital projects, with significant project and contract management responsibility.
Direct experience working on project-financed projects, including lender due diligence, , funding drawdowns, lender technical adviser processes and ongoing lender / investor reporting.
Strong understanding of the Client / Employer’s Representative role and experience representing an owner, SPV, sponsor or employer in the delivery of complex contracted projects.
Extensive experience administering FIDIC, EPC, ICP and construction management contracts, including notices, variations, claims, payment mechanisms, completion tests, liquidated damages and contractual close-out.
Demonstrable ability to lead multidisciplinary internal teams and align finance, legal, engineering, procurement, construction, operations and external adviser inputs around delivery milestones within a standardised delivery framework.
Strong commercial and financial acumen, with the ability to assess risk versus reward, protect the employer’s position and communicate implications clearly to senior stakeholders.
Experience preparing and presenting concise, decision-ready reports for senior management, investment committees, SPV boards, lenders, investors, shareholder forums and other governance forums, with the ability to translate complex programme, commercial, technical and financing issues into clear options and recommendations.
Working knowledge of utility-scale solar PV, BESS, grid connection and route-to-market interfaces, with sufficient technical understanding to challenge contractors and advisers effectively.
Highly organised and proficient in Microsoft Office and project controls tools, with strong written communication, meeting management and stakeholder engagement skills.
Valid driver’s license for Ireland and the UK.

Build strong working relationships with internal and external partners.
Support and train additional team members as needed.
Contribute to process improvement initiatives that simplify workflows and eliminate inefficiencies.
Take on ad‑hoc tasks and diverse projects with a solutions‑oriented mindset.

Strong project management skills and comfort leading cross‑functional efforts
Experience leveraging AI in the contracts and budgets space

2+ years of experience working in a fast paced and volume driven work environment

WSP ist eines der weltweit führenden Ingenieurunternehmen mit den Geschäftsbereichen Infrastruktur, Verkehr, Umwelt, Energie und Gebäude.
Unsere Vision ist klar: Wir wollen die Welt zu einem besseren Ort machen, indem wir einen positiven Beitrag zur Gesellschaft leisten und nachhaltige Lösungen für die Herausforderungen der Zukunft entwickeln.
Stellen Sie sich eine bessere Zukunft für uns alle vor – und eine bessere Zukunft für Sie.
Zur Verstärkung unserer Einheit Transport & Infrastructure suchen wir für die Niederlassung in Luzern oder Zürich eine(n)
Bauleiter*in im Strassen- und Tiefbau (80-100%)
In dieser Rolle wirst du Teil eines interdisziplinären Teams, das die Grundwerte unseres Unternehmens verkörpert: Zusammenarbeit, Leidenschaft für komplexe Projekte und Innovationsgeist.

s.h: DEINE NEUE ROLLE – DAS GEHÖRT DAZU
s.t:
Du arbeitest eng mit den Projektleitenden und dem Projektierungsteam zusammen und sorgst mit einer offenen Kommunikation und strukturierten Koordination für reibungslose Abläufe im Projekt
Du erstellst präzise Submissionsunterlagen und Leistungsverzeichnisse und stellst sicher, dass alle Dokumente fachgerecht und vollständig ausgearbeitet sind
Du leitest als Bauleiter vor Ort innerstädtische sowie kantonale Strassenbau‑ und Tiefbauprojekte im Grossraum LU / ZH / AG
Du koordinierst Unternehmer, Behörden und Projektbeteiligte in der Ausführung und hältst die Fäden zusammen – auf der Baustelle und im Büro
Du stellst über den Bauablauf sicher, dass Termine, Qualität und Kosten eingehalten werden und unterstützt die Projektleitung im Projektabschluss
Du unterstützt das Projektteam in frühen Projektphasen bei der Planung der Bauphasen und Verkehrsführung sowie Kostenschätzungen

Das Team Transport und Infrastruktur in der Deutschschweiz umfasst diverse Fachdisziplinen (Strasseninfrastruktur und Verkehr, Bahnbau, Untertagebau, BSA, Kunstbauten, Siedlungsentwässerung) und arbeitet eng mit Kollegen der BHU, Hochbau, Nachhaltigkeit, BIM u.a. im In- und Ausland zusammen. Das Kernteam Strassen- und Tiefbau umfasst ca. 25 Personen, verteilt primär auf die Niederlassungen Luzern und Zürich.

Du hast eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung als dipl. Techniker*in, Bauleiter*in, einen Abschluss in Bauingenieurwesen (ETH/FH) oder eine gleichwertige Qualifikation
Du bringst mehrere Jahre Erfahrung im Tiefbau mit und verfügst über fundierte Fachkenntnisse
Du engagierst dich mit hohen Verantwortungsbewusstsein gegenüber deinem Team sowie unseren Kunden
Du hast sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (von Vorteil: gute Englischkenntnisse)
Du bearbeitest deine Leistungspakete selbstständig und unterstützt deine Kolleginnen und Kollegen gerne mit deiner Erfahrung
Du bist offen für Innovation und unterstützt die Weiterentwicklung von internen Standards und Prozessen (BIM, Lean Management, papierlose Baustelle, etc.)

s.h: WAS DIR BEI UNS GEFALLEN WIRD
s.t:
Ein Arbeitsumfeld, das von Vielfalt inspiriert und von Inklusion motiviert ist
Unsere flexible Arbeitspolitik – wir erkennen die Bedeutung einer ausgewogenen Work-Life-Balance an und ermutigen Dich, Deine eigene zu finden
Die Möglichkeit, an grossen Infrastrukturprojekten mitzuwirken und mitzuerleben, wie aus deiner Arbeit konkrete und sichtbare Bauwerke entstehen
Ausgezeichnete Karriereperspektiven – wir entwickeln uns schnell weiter und streben jeden Tag danach, uns selbst zu verbessern. Wir sind offen für Deine Ideen und wollen neue Dinge ausprobieren, und wir bieten Dir ein positives Umfeld, das in Deine Entwicklung und Ausbildung investiert
WSP steht für eine Kultur der Zusammenarbeit mit Kollegen, die sich durch ihre Fähigkeiten auszeichnen – lerne unser fantastisches Team kennen!
WSP leistet überdurchschnittliche Sozialleistungen (zusätzliche Kinderzulagen und höhere PK-Beiträge)

Unsere engagierten Mitarbeiter*innen haben das gemeinsame Ziel, durch eine Kultur der Innovation, Integrität und Inklusion einen positiven und dauerhaften Einfluss auf die Gesellschaften, für die wir tätig sind, auszuüben.
Unser Bewerbungsprozess umfasst drei Schritte: ein telefonischer Austausch, gefolgt von zwei Vorstellungsgesprächen – und bei positivem Verlauf erhältst du unser Angebot!.

## Description de l'entreprise ##
Notre client est un acteur établi du secteur de la construction en Suisse romande. Grâce à son expertise technique, à ses équipes expérimentées et à sa capacité à réaliser des projets d'envergure, l'entreprise intervient sur des chantiers variés dans le domaine du terrassement et des infrastructures.

Elle propose un environnement dynamique, axé sur la qualité, la sécurité et l'efficacité opérationnelle, au sein duquel chaque collaborateur bénéficie d'un réel niveau d'autonomie et de responsabilités.
## Description du poste ##
Dans le cadre de vos fonctions, vous serez responsable de la préparation, de l'organisation et du suivi complet de vos chantiers de terrassement, de la phase de préparation jusqu'à leur réalisation finale.
* Préparer les chantiers sur les plans technique, organisationnel et financier.
* Planifier les différentes étapes des travaux, notamment les besoins en personnel, en matériel et en équipements.
* Organiser le déroulement quotidien des chantiers et assurer leur exécution opérationnelle.
* Coordonner les équipes, les sous-traitants et les différents intervenants.
* Assurer la commande, l'approvisionnement et la disponibilité des matériaux et équipements nécessaires.
* Mettre en place et suivre les procédures liées à la qualité, à la sécurité et à l'environnement.
* Contrôler l'avancement des travaux ainsi que le respect des délais et des coûts.
* Assurer le suivi financier des chantiers.
* Élaborer les offres, les offres complémentaires et les métrés des travaux réalisés.
* Participer à la facturation et au contrôle des prestations exécutées.
* Participer aux séances de chantier et assurer le suivi des décisions prises.
* Entretenir une relation professionnelle de qualité avec les maîtres d'ouvrage, les directions de travaux et les partenaires du projet.
## Profil recherché ##
* Vous êtes titulaire d'une formation reconnue de conducteur(trice) de travaux.
* Vous justifiez d'au moins **5 ans d'expérience confirmée dans la conduite de chantiers en Suisse.**
* Vous disposez d'une expérience concrète dans le domaine du terrassement.
* Vous maîtrisez les outils informatiques usuels ainsi que le logiciel BauBit.
* Vous êtes à l'aise dans le suivi technique, administratif et financier des chantiers.
* Vous êtes une personne proactive, autonome, organisée et dotée d'un bon sens des responsabilités.
* Vous appréciez le travail en équipe et savez communiquer efficacement avec les différents intervenants d'un chantier.

**Megasol Energie AG** fait partie des principaux fabricants suisses de modules solaires innovants et de solutions photovoltaïques intégrées aux bâtiments. À notre siège principal à Deitingen, nous réunissons développement, production, vente et logistique sous un même toit.
Pour diriger notre service commercial interne, nous recherchons une personne qui ne se contente pas de prendre des responsabilités, mais qui les revendique activement. Vous veillez à ce que les offres, commandes, planifications et envois internationaux soient traités rapidement, de manière fiable et évolutive. En même temps, vous développez votre département de manière organisationnelle et digitale de façon cohérente.
Ce poste s'adresse à des personnes qui ont des exigences élevées envers leur propre performance, qui aiment façonner les choses et ne laissent pas les résultats au hasard.
### **Vos responsabilités** ###
Vous dirigez le service commercial interne sur le plan professionnel, personnel et organisationnel et êtes responsable de la performance, de la qualité et de la fiabilité de votre département.

En même temps, vous faites partie intégrante des opérations quotidiennes, travaillez activement en équipe chaque jour et assumez la responsabilité en cas de situations critiques, de goulets d'étranglement et d'escalades.

Ainsi, vous connaissez les processus de première main, détectez rapidement les points faibles et développez votre équipe de manière cohérente.

* Responsabilité globale du service commercial interne, de la planification ainsi que de la gestion des commandes et des offres
* Participation opérationnelle continue aux offres, commandes, planifications et demandes clients
* Assurer un traitement rapide, correct et contraignant des commandes
* Gestion de l'équipe selon des objectifs clairs, des responsabilités et des standards de performance mesurables
* Développement ciblé des collaborateurs pour constituer une équipe compétente et autonome
* Coordination des envois nationaux et internationaux, y compris la documentation complète d'expédition, d'exportation et de dédouanement

* Numérisation et optimisation des processus avec des améliorations mesurables en qualité, rapidité et transparence
